La musique Manjak est au cœur de toute c: Manjak music is at the heart of every ceremony. The drums speak — each rhythm carries a message. The balafon (a xylophone with wooden bars) and the kora (a 21-string harp-lute) accompany ritual dances and celebrations.
La religion traditionnelle Manjak est an: The traditional Manjak religion is animist: the spirits of the ancestors (bëpëk) guide the living. Ceremonies and sacrifices make it possible to communicate with these spirits. Part of the population has adopted Islam or Christianity.
Les rites de passage marquent la transit: Rites of passage mark the transition to adulthood. For boys, the fanado (initiation) is a period of retreat in the forest where they learn their social responsibilities. For girls, ceremonies celebrate fertility and feminine wisdom.
Les Manjak sont réputés pour leurs texti: The Manjak are renowned for their textiles with colourful geometric patterns, their fine basketry and their pottery. These arts carry symbolic codes linked to clans, social status and the farming seasons.
Agriculteurs et pêcheurs par excellence,: Farmers and fishers above all, the Manjak have developed highly sophisticated systems of terraced rice farming and estuary fishing. Rice growing is closely tied to their identity and their rituals.
La mémoire Manjak est orale. Les griots: Manjak memory is oral. Griots and storytellers pass on the history, philosophy and values of the people through elaborate tales, vivid proverbs and sung epics that can last several nights.
La société Manjak est organisée en clans: Manjak society is organised into clans (badjak) and matrilineal lineages. Each clan has its own chief, its animal totem and its food taboos. Marriage alliances between clans ensure peace and social cohesion.
Manjak en Europe & dans le monde: Manjak in Europe & around the world
Une importante diaspora Manjak vit en Eu: A large Manjak diaspora lives in Europe — Portugal, France, Sweden, Spain, Italy. These communities keep Manjak culture alive abroad: tontines, cultural associations, remittances and a connection with the homeland.
Les Manjak (ou Manjaku, Manjaco) sont un: The Manjak (or Manjaku, Manjaco) are a West African people belonging to the West Atlantic language group. Their origins go back to the peoples of Senegambia, a coastal region between the Senegal and Gambia rivers.
Peuple autochtone de la côte ouest-afric: An indigenous people of the West African coast, the Manjak have lived on the fertile lands of present-day Guinea-Bissau, Senegal and The Gambia for thousands of years. They are deeply tied to the land, the sea and the mangrove forests.
Leur nom 'Manjak' viendrait du terme 'Ma: Their name 'Manjak' is said to come from the term 'Manjaku', literally meaning 'the people of the waters' — a reference to their historical closeness to coastal areas, estuaries and flooded rice fields.
Durant la période médiévale, les Manjak: During the medieval period, the Manjak were part of the trade networks of Senegambia. They traded rice, salt, cloth and iron with the Mandé, Wolof, Diola and Fula peoples.
Les Manjak ont résisté à l'expansion des: The Manjak resisted the expansion of the great Sahelian empires — Ghana, Mali — thanks to their hard-to-reach coastal position. Their organisation into decentralised clans gave them great resilience against conquest.
Les royaumes Beafada et Bijagos voisins: The neighbouring Beafada and Bijagos kingdoms maintained relations of trade and sometimes conflict with the Manjak communities, forging a distinct identity between people of the coast and people of the forest.
L'arrivée des Portugais et la traite nég: The arrival of the Portuguese and the slave trade
Les premiers contacts avec les Européens: The first contacts with Europeans took place in the 15th century, when Portuguese explorers reached the coast of Guinea. The Portuguese set up trading posts at Cacheu and Bissau, in the heart of Manjak territory.
Les Manjak figurent parmi les peuples d': The Manjak are among the West African peoples who were victims of the transatlantic slave trade. Thousands of Manjak were torn from their lands and deported to the Americas, particularly Brazil and the Caribbean.
Malgré la violence de la colonisation, l: Despite the violence of colonisation, the Manjak kept their cultural identity. Some Manjak chiefs negotiated with the Portuguese to limit the raids; others organised armed resistance. The Manjaku language survived intact.
Sous la colonisation portugaise de Guiné: Under the Portuguese colonisation of Guinea-Bissau (then Portuguese Guinea), the Manjak resisted taxation and forced labour. Several uprisings took place between 1880 and 1920 in the Cacheu and Oio regions.
La colonisation imposa une administratio: Colonisation imposed a centralised administration that upset traditional social structures. Manjak clan chiefs were either co-opted as intermediaries (régulos) or persecuted. The Catholic Church set up missions, bringing education in Portuguese.
Paradoxalement, l'alphabétisation en por: Paradoxically, literacy in Portuguese allowed a generation of Manjak to gain access to world literature and to defend their rights. Manjak people took an active part in the independence movement led by Amilcar Cabral (PAIGC).
La Guinée-Bissau obtient son indépendanc: Guinea-Bissau gained its independence from Portugal on 24 September 1974, after an eleven-year war of liberation. The Manjak, present throughout the territory, took part in this struggle for dignity and self-determination.
Depuis l'indépendance, les communautés M: Since independence, Manjak communities have worked to revitalise their language and culture. Linguists, working with the elders, have begun to standardise the Manjaku alphabet — work that continues today.
La diaspora Manjak en Europe (Portugal,: The Manjak diaspora in Europe (Portugal, France, Sweden, Spain) plays a crucial role in this revival: organising cultural festivals, passing the language on to children born abroad, and funding educational projects in Guinea-Bissau and Senegal.
Aujourd'hui, les anciens Manjak développ: Today, the Manjak elders are developing an alphabet of their own for their language — unique symbols that capture the sounds and the soul of an Atlantic language thousands of years old. This project is the digital continuation of that essential work.

La tradition orale Manjak est immense —: The Manjak oral tradition is immense — tales, family epics, ritual songs. This project aims to document and digitise this priceless heritage.
Instrument central des cérémonies Manjak: The central instrument of Manjak ceremonies. Each rhythm carries a coded message. The drummers are respected griots.
Xylophone à lames de bois avec calebasse: A xylophone with wooden bars and resonating calabashes. Its crystal-clear sound accompanies harvest festivals and funerals.
Harpe-luth à 21 cordes partagée avec les: A 21-string harp-lute shared with the Mandé peoples. The storytelling instrument above all others, it sings the history of the clans.

Rite d'initiation masculin. Les jeunes g: Male initiation rite. The young boys are taught by the elders about the responsibilities of a Manjak man: courage, respect for the ancestors, knowledge of the traditions.
Cérémonies célébrant la transition des j: Ceremonies celebrating the transition of young girls. Teachings on feminine wisdom and the passing on of craft skills.
Les funérailles Manjak peuvent durer plu: Manjak funerals can last several days. The ancestors are venerated and their spirit (bëpëk) is invoked. Music and dance allow the soul of the deceased to join the ancestors.
Avant les semailles du riz et après la r: Before the rice is sown and after the harvest, ceremonies of thanks to the spirits of the land are held.
Le mariage Manjak est une affaire de cla: Manjak marriage is a matter between clans. The dowry strengthens alliances between lineages. The festivities last several days, with music and ritual dances.
Pratique de vénération — on verse de l'a: A practice of veneration — palm alcohol is poured on the ground to call the spirits of the ancestors and ask them for protection and wisdom.
Tissus à bandes colorées aux motifs géom: Cloth in colourful strips with geometric patterns. Each pattern has a meaning: clan, social status, festive occasion or mourning.
Les paniers et nattes tressés par les fe: The baskets and mats woven by Manjak women are renowned for their fineness. They serve as containers, decorations and prestige gifts.
An ancestral art passed down from mother to daughter. Manjak pottery is decorated with incised patterns and polished by hand.
Malgré des siècles de pressions extérieu: Despite centuries of outside pressure — the slave trade, Portuguese colonisation — the Manjak people have preserved their culture, their language and their identity.
